title: What the Java Memory Model is made of

questions.stem: Per this page, in what terms does the current JMM (JLS §17.4) define its guarantees?

options.text: Main memory, a working memory per thread, and flushes between them
options.says: The page calls main and working memory a mental model that the pre-Java 5 JMM used; the current JMM defines no memory regions.

options.text: CPU caches, registers, and the memory barriers placed between them
options.says: The page says the JMM is an abstraction that defines no memory regions or caches, not a description of hardware.

options.text: Actions, program order, synchronization order and happens-before
options.says: The page says the current JMM is defined through actions, program order, synchronization order and happens-before.

questions.stem: Per this page, which choice fits a shared counter that many threads bump, where no update may be lost and no lock is taken?

options.says: The page says volatile gives visibility only and that i++ is a read-modify-write, so volatile does not make it atomic.
The page's Q3 answer names AtomicInteger for atomicity without a lock, and its atomic operations are both atomic and visible.
The page says a plain long is not even guaranteed atomic to read or write, and += is a compound operation.
